stories.headline: Govt calls for climate-resilient flood measures
stories.title: Govt calls for climate-resilient flood measures
stories.summary: Jammu,Oct 18: Minister for Jal Shakti, Forest, Ecology & Environment and Tribal Affairs, Javed Ahmed Rana, on Sunday inaugurated flood protection works worth ₹5.91 crore along vulnerable stretches of River Nikki Tawi and River Waddi Tawi in Jammu, underscoring Government’s commitment to strengthening flood management infrastructure, enhancing climate resilience and safeguarding vulnerable habitations, agricultural land and public infrastructure. The projects, funded under the Special Assistance to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) scheme and NABARD, are aimed at mitigating riverbank erosion, reducing flood risks and strengthening protective infrastructure in areas vulnerable to rising water levels and heavy river discharge during periods of intense rainfall. The inauguration of the respective works was attended by MLA, Bahu, Ch. Vikram Randhawa, and MLA, Marh, Surinder Kumar. Emphasising the need for a proactive and sustainable approach to flood management in the face of changing climatic conditions, Rana said that preventive measures, timely interventions and resilient infrastructure were essential to minimise the impact of natural disasters on lives, livelihoods and public assets. “As we witness increasingly erratic weather patterns and climate-related challenges, strengthening our preparedness against floods has become imperative. Our priority must be to protect vulnerable riverbanks, safeguard habitations and agricultural land, and ensure that critical public infrastructure remains secure. Effective flood management requires advance planning, sound engineering interventions and sustained efforts to reduce risks before disasters strike,” the Minister said. The Minister stressed that all flood protection works must adhere to prescribed technical standards and quality benchmarks, with particular emphasis on durability, long-term sustainability and timely execution. He said the Government was committed to strengthening protective infrastructure in vulnerable areas and ensuring that development initiatives translated into tangible and lasting benefits for local communities. The first project, completed at an estimated cost of ₹229.94 lakh under SASCI, involves flood protection measures along the left bank of River Nikki Tawi downstream of the 4th Bridge at Belicharana. The work targets vulnerable stretches susceptible to erosion and flooding, with the objective of protecting nearby habitations, agricultural land and public infrastructure, particularly during the monsoon season. MLA Bahu, Vikram Randhawa, was present at the inauguration of this project. The second intervention, estimated to cost ₹69 lakh under SASCI, involves the construction of two spurs, each measuring 18 metres in length, along the left side of River Waddi Tawi at Channi Nankey, Nandni. The spurs are designed to help regulate river flow near vulnerable stretches, reduce the risk of bank erosion and provide greater protection to adjoining agricultural land, settlements and public assets. Rana stressed that the remaining work should be completed on priority to ensure that the intended benefits reach the people without delay. The third project, estimated at ₹292 lakh and funded under NABARD, comprises flood protection measures along the right side of River Nikki Tawi, extending from Omman Post to Makwal Forward Post in village Makwal. The inauguration of this work was attended by MLA Marh, Surinder Kumar. The project includes the construction of revetment crates and earthen embankments at vulnerable locations to reinforce the riverbank, check erosion and reduce the risk of flooding. The intervention is particularly significant for protecting adjoining agricultural land and local infrastructure in the border village, where effective flood protection is essential for safeguarding livelihoods and community assets. Highlighting the importance of preparedness and coordinated action in disaster management, Rana called for close coordination among the concerned departments, regular monitoring of project implementation and adherence to prescribed quality standards. He said that sustained supervision was necessary to ensure the effectiveness of flood protection measures, especially in areas exposed to recurring flooding and riverbank erosion. Rana further underscored the importance of completing ongoing works within stipulated timelines, directing that implementation be closely monitored to avoid unnecessary delays. He said that timely completion, coupled with quality construction and effective maintenance, would be crucial to ensuring that the intended benefits of these projects were realised on the ground. By improving protective infrastructure in strategically important locations, the projects are aimed at reducing risks to nearby communities, agricultural activities and public assets. The initiatives reflect the Government’s continued focus on strengthening flood management systems, improving disaster preparedness and promoting climate-resilient infrastructure across Jammu and Kashmir.

stories.headline: Europe refused China, India oil sanctions
stories.title: Europe refused China, India oil sanctions
stories.summary: Washington, Amid intense criticism, the US on Sunday said the waiver of sanctions on Russia and tariffs on other countries, including India, was a 60-day pause to analyse the global impact of the measure.Trump's cabinet colleagues Marco Rubio and Scott Bessent said the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act granted the President the flexibility to assess the situation."No sanctions were lifted on Friday," Bessent told NBC's Meet the Press, referring to the Executive Order signed by Trump granting a waiver from sanctions under the Graham Act passed with overwhelming bipartisan support last month.Bessent revealed that the US had asked its European allies to impose secondary sanctions on China and India for buying Russian oil, but they refused."So why should the US bear the burden? President Trump, perhaps we will be in contact with our European partners. Why should the US go it alone," Bessent said, adding that European countries had waived an embargo on purchase of Russian diesel and jet fuel in May.On Saturday evening, Secretary of State Rubio said waivers were included in the Graham Act to study the different things going around the world, such as the pressure on global energy supplies due to the Iran war, the attack of Houthis in Saudi Arabia and the Ukraine-Russia war."I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy, and even to the US economy," Rubio told reporters before leaving on a six-day visit to Uzbekistan and India.The executive order signed by Trump on Friday states that the waivers shall remain in effect until such time as the President or the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury and the Trade Representative, as appropriate, determine that further action is appropriate.Speaking to reporters at Mar-a-Lago resort near Miami on Saturday, Trump said his decision to waive sanctions under the Graham Act would benefit the US."A lot of you don't know what my decision is yet, but we'll figure it out, and you'll figure it out," he said."It's a very good decision, and it's going to be a decision that's good for the country, and I think good for the world because we're really at a world stage," Trump said.Bessent also accused the European nations of fuelling Russia's war on Ukraine by buying oil and gas from Moscow."The Europeans have given Russia and Vladimir Putin more money than they've given the Ukrainians. They continue to gorge on Russian energy," Bessent said."The Europeans are financing the Russian war machine. The US imports USD four billion of Russian products. USD 1.8 billion of that is fertiliser. The Europeans import more than 10 times that," Bessent said.Trump's decision to waive sanctions on Russia came under fire from the Republicans and Democrats, who last month came together to overwhelmingly pass the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.Senator Darline Graham, a Republican from South Carolina, also criticised Trump for exempting Russia from a sanctions law that was championed by and named after her late brother Lindsey.Indian-American lawmakers, most of whom had voted against the Graham Act, were sharply critical of Trump's decision."Trump's decision to waive new sanctions on Russia should leave no doubt: that is exactly what is happening," Congressman Ami Bera said on X."My Republican colleagues pushed hard to pass the Lindsey Graham Russia sanctions bill before we left town. They ought to be standing up and screaming at the top of their lungs that we don't side with Russia," he said."Trump is doing exactly what we warned: undermining Congress' authority, abandoning Ukraine, and letting Putin off the hook," Congressman Suhas Subramanyam said on X."Republicans refused to let us vote on stronger Russia sanctions. Now we - and our allies - are paying the price," Subramanyam said.

stories.title: Delhi Cabinet clears plan to create ₹50-cr. corpus for start-ups

candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The Delhi government has approved the setting up of the Go-Delhi Foundation, an initiative aimed at promoting startups, innovation and entrepreneurship in the capital.

The foundation will provide young people, researchers and entrepreneurs with integrated support to turn their ideas into practical products and successful enterprises, the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO) said in a statement on Sunday.
It will have an initial budgetary outlay of ₹50 crore.
The Cabinet, chaired by Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, recently approved the foundation and sanctioned funds to help turn ideas into products and bring them to market.
Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the initiative is an important step towards bringing together Delhi’s existing entrepreneurial capabilities, educational institutions and research facilities.
“Delhi has nearly 21,000 start-ups recognised by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT).

Through the Go-Delhi Foundation, these resources will be brought together on a common platform, with a focus on developing new enterprises, attracting investment and creating employment opportunities,” she said.
The foundation will help startups and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) access product engineering, prototyping, laboratory and testing facilities.
It will also offer mentorship and support entrepreneurs at different stages, from product development and testing to certification preparation and market access, Ms. Gupta said.
The foundation will be established as a not-for-profit company under Section 8 of the Companies Act, 2013, and function under the Delhi government’s Department of Industries.
Government departments will be able to bring their real-world challenges to Delhi’s innovators through the foundation, Ms. Gupta said.
Products and technologies developed to address these challenges could be tested through pilot projects, with successful solutions taken forward for adoption.

stories.headline: Historic High Court bench opens in Ladakh
stories.title: Historic High Court bench opens in Ladakh
stories.summary: Leh, Oct 18: In a significant step towards strengthening access to justice in the Union Territory, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Justice Surya Kant inaugurated the Ladakh Bench of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh in Leh, marking a historic milestone for the region’s judicial system. The inauguration took place in the presence of judges of the Supreme Court and the Chief Justice and other judges of the High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. Welcoming the development, Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh V.K. Saxena said the establishment of the Bench fulfils a long-standing demand of the people and will bring justice closer to their doorsteps. The move is expected to ease the burden of long-distance travel and related expenses for litigants who previously had to travel outside Ladakh for High Court-related proceedings. The Lieutenant Governor also highlighted that the CJI’s successive visits to Ladakh within a span of six months reflect a continued focus on improving access to justice, particularly for communities living in remote and geographically challenging areas. Saxena expressed gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah for their guidance and support towards Ladakh’s development. The inauguration marks an important development for Ladakh, with the new Bench expected to improve geographical access to the High Court and strengthen the delivery of justice in the region.
